title: GTA 6: The Blockbuster That is Changing Gaming Forever
summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the biggest entertainment releases in recent history. But can one blockbuster video game revive an industry facing layoffs, consolidation and slowing consumer spending? NYU Stern professor Joost van Dreunen and Griffin Gaming Partners’ Nick Tuosto examine what GTA 6 means for developers, distributors, industry consolidation and investment opportunities for this hundred billion-dollar industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Confronts AI Reality Check
summary: Bloomberg US equities reporter Natalia Kniazhevich tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Anthropic’s record IPO failed to reverse deteriorating market sentiment as investors grapple with Nvidia turmoil, AI spending concerns and selling by systematic funds. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kniazhevich explains why Goldman Sachs’ Panic Index has reached 9 out of 10 and what heavy positioning, weak liquidity and a wave of potential new stock issuance could mean for markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple TV 4K Review: New $299 Streaming Box is Excellent But Too Expensive
summary: At $299, the company’s excellent set-top box is suddenly hard to recommend.

title: China Plans to Strengthen AI Token Standards in Computing Push
summary: China’s National Data Administration will improve standards on the measurement and billing of artificial intelligence tokens and quality assessment, as Beijing guides the development of the growing industry.

title: How AI Is Reshaping China's Industrial Policy
summary: Can Chinese tech companies help the country achieve technological self-reliance while keeping up in the AI arms race? On this episode, we speak with Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center and author of the High Capacity newsletter, about Beijing’s response to the global AI boom and the tensions between Chinese companies’ commercial ambitions and the government’s long-term plans. He explains how companies draw on shared expertise and supply chains to expand across industries including smartphones, robotics, EVs and semiconductors — and we also discuss Huawei’s efforts to compete with Nvidia and why technological success doesn’t necessarily translate into strong returns for stock investors in China.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Taiwan Widens Short Sale Curbs After Shares Plunge on AI Concern
summary: Taiwan widened curbs on short sales of local stocks and said it has been buying shares, stepping up efforts to revive confidence after the island’s benchmark index had its worst weekly fall in 35 years.

title: China Deploys 5G Across Manufacturing Base as 6G Testing Advances, CCTV Reports
summary: China is expanding the use of 5G across its manufacturing sector, with more than 26,000 private industrial 5G networks built nationwide, China Central Television said on Saturday.

title: Anthropic Researcher Claims to Solve Riemann Problem With Claude
summary: On the heels of Anthropic PBC’s record-breaking initial public offering, a researcher at the company said he believes he used its artificial intelligence software to solve a famous number theory problem that has plagued mathematicians for more than 150 years.

title: Wall Street Week | Gaming Blockbuster, Healthcare Costs, Cybersecurity Meets AI
summary: This week, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss what the Treasury and Fed can do to tackle the nation’s debt crisis. Plus, what Grand Theft Auto 6’s release means for a video game industry that routinely faces layoffs, delays and slowing consumer spending. Later, surging healthcare costs affect businesses and their employees as Americans choose their insurance policies for the year ahead. And, how is AI changing the cybersecurity stakes for small businesses? (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tony Wang on CrowdStrike-Zscaler Deal, AI Trade
summary: Tony Wang, Portfolio Manager of the Science and Technology Equity Strategy at T. Rowe Price, is asked whether the AI cycle has changed and whether recent declines create a buying opportunity. He also flags Wednesday’s PCE inflation report as a potential catalyst for markets. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wonder Explores Sale of Delivery Service Grubhub, WSJ Reports
summary: Grubhub owner Wonder is considering a sale of the food-delivery business, the Wall Street Journal reported, adding to a wave of dealmaking in the sector.

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Drives Internet Providers to Record Usage
summary: Record demand for the hot new video game Grand Theft Auto VI sent US internet traffic soaring this week.

title: Hindlian Advisory CEO on AI & Anthropic Market Sell-off
summary: Amanda Hindlian, Founder and CEO of Hindlian Advisory and Former Global Head of Capital Markets at the New York Stock Exchange, says Anthropic’s IPO should be judged separately from a volatile week for markets. She notes that investors had been uncertain about the pricing and overall execution just two weeks earlier, but the offering priced well, drew a significantly oversubscribed book—estimated at five to seven times—and traded strongly on its first day. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Scribe CEO Jennifer Smith on AI Usage in the Workplace
summary: Jennifer Smith, Co-Founder and CEO of Scribe and a former Consultant at McKinsey, discusses AI valuations to adoption, noting research that puts AI use for workplace tasks below 4%. She says the findings contrast with the widespread chatbot and AI use they observe in their own circle. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cognition in Talks for $75 Billion Value With New Funding
summary: Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, just two months after announcing its most recent funding round, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: CrowdStrike Is in Talks to Buy Cybersecurity Firm Zscaler
summary: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. is in talks to acquire Zscaler Inc., according to people familiar with the matter, in a deal that would be among the largest-ever in the cybersecurity sector.

title: US Credit-Fear Hits 8-Month High as Tech Angst Roils Markets
summary: Measures of perceived US credit risk reached levels not seen in nearly eight months and the cost of protecting the debt of some of the biggest tech firms against default jumped on Friday, as the wobbling AI trade spurred volatility in global markets and sent investors piling into safe havens.

title: Emerging Stocks Enter Bear Market as AI Triggers Global Selloff
summary: The MSCI emerging-market stock index entered a bear market Friday, declining for a seventh day, the longest losing streak since 2024, amid a selloff in global tech shares.

title: Victor Peng Sees AI, Quantum Computing as Long-Term Opportunities
summary: Victor Peng, CEO of PsiQuantum and former Advanced Micro Devices president, says quantum computing and optical switching could lower compute costs on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
summary: Wall Street reeled on Friday as nagging concerns about the AI trade, which propelled US stocks from one high to the next for much of the year, turned into a full-blown, market-wide selloff. Anthropic PBC slumped after soaring in its public-market debut, while Nvidia Corp. sank 14%, pushing the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.
